Controlling grass starts with good soil prep, before you plant make sure the area is cleared and tilled, pulling out grass by the roots, some of the grass I dug out when getting my bed ready this year had roots a foot deep! Make sure do to it when the soil is really moist it helps get the roots out without breaking them. Adding some kind of ground covering is also really important, straw, hay, or some kind of mulch over your beds helps control weeds and grass really well and has the added benefit of keeping moisture in the soil, you can even use plastic or landscape fabric if you want almost total weed control. Making sure the surrounding grass stays trimmed and cut short is important too, if its too much of a problem you can try killing it with vinegar, or pouring boiling water on it, there are also chemicals but because its so close to your plants I personally wouldn't use them. You're most likely never going to prevent it from spreading and growing completely but those things I listed can help you control it.
